test: real Claude Code and Codex remote capture recover after HTTP outage and server restart
limitations: Both authenticated clients and the server ran on one physical machine; cross-machine network transit and TLS were NOT_RUN.
The Claude CLI invocation took 373 seconds. A globally installed claude-mem SessionEnd hook was observed in the process tree; this is external host-hook latency, not an Engram timeout.
Physical cross-machine delivery was not run; container results are reported as a separate tier and do not satisfy that requirement.
Hanging-connection (packet drop), packet loss, clock skew and real WAN paths were not exercised.

singleMachineLive.note: PRIOR evidence from Agent A (live Claude Code + Codex, one machine). Not re-run on the combined tree.

topology.tls: test CA (ECDSA P-256), node TLS terminator -> loopback HTTP upstream

isolatedContainers.note: Fresh run on the combined A+B+C tree. Hooks are the installed adapter commands with real-format payloads; live Claude Code/Codex binaries are not run in containers.

physicalHosts.blocker: No separate physical hosts are configured or authorized; no SSH hosts exist in the user configuration and none were contacted.

defectsFound.finding: 1100 concurrent hook processes left 1002 entries in a spool capped at 1000 (check-then-write race).
defectsFound.fix: packages/memory/remote-spool.ts re-checks after publishing and withdraws its own entry when over the cap.
defectsFound.regression: tests/memory/remote-spool.test.ts (fails with 1030 entries without the fix)

defectsFound.finding: Under full-suite load a drain failed with ENOENT/EINVAL writing drain.lock/owner.json: a contender saw the freshly created lock directory without its owner file, judged it stale and deleted it. Also, if every acquisition attempt failed the drain work could run without holding the lock.
defectsFound.fix: packages/memory/capture.ts: a missing owner file is treated as a drain still starting (bounded 300 ms grace, immediate if the lock is already gone); a drain whose lock vanished retries; work runs only when the lock was acquired.
defectsFound.regression: tests/memory/capture.test.ts "concurrent drains never fail on the lock" (fails on the old code in round 0)
defectsFound.code: present in both Agent A and B+C code before this fix

observations: The client has no retry timer or backoff: delivery is attempted on each hook invocation and on explicit `mdb memory drain-remote`, each attempt bounded to 2 s and 100 envelopes. A backlog (including a SessionEnd) is therefore delivered at the next hook or explicit drain after connectivity returns, not autonomously.
The server acknowledges with 202 once the event is in its durable spool and commits asynchronously; delivery is final only when its spool is empty.
Hooks are silent by design; the client-visible signal is spool depth.
Untested: a permanently rejected envelope at the head of a spool blocks later envelopes (the drain stops at the first non-OK response).
